statement.text:
This problem presents several variations on the Cosmetic
Surgery Conjecture, discussed in turn below.
(a) $($ Cosmetic Surgery Conjecture $)$ Two surgeries along inequivalent slopes are
never purely cosmetic.
(b) $($ Oriented knot complement conjecture $)$ If $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ are knots in a closed,
oriented 3-manifold $N$ whose complements are homeomorphic via an orientation-
preserving homeomorphism, then there exists a homeomorphism of $N$ tak-
ing $K_{1}$ to $K_{2}$.
(c) Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a nontrivial knot, then $K$ admits no purely cosmetic surg-
eries.
(d) If $K \subset S^{3}$ is not the torus knot $T_{2g+1,2}$, then $K$ admits no chirally cos-
metic surgeries with inequivalent slopes.
